findings.text: The new `kid.replay_end?.()` in `core/Task/Task.js:513` runs after `store.attach(kid)` and outside `Store.replay_depth`, so the state it infers is recorded as a delta and appended to the referenced folder's own file. Every browser that opens a session page would then write `{"set":{"state":…}}` into every task folder that session references. Fix: run it inside `Store.replay_depth++ … finally --` (as `Item.replay` and the snapshot branch of `Store.attach` already do). Then add a test that a browser-path open writes nothing.

This has already happened to real data. The agent's shot script (transcript 23:02:30) routed the worktree's `Task.js` into the live main site, and at 23:02:50–54 one client (`d6aa194c`, stamped `by: owner`) appended a `set state` line to 41 records under `sessions/2026/10/20/session-e00f55c9/` and `2026/11/02/` (e.g. `dictate-plugins/session.jsonl` and this task's own `session.jsonl`). One of those lines is `state: stopped` with a `stopped_at`. Those lines need finding by `"client":"d6aa194c"` and moving aside (not deleting), and the shot should have come from the worktree's own server rather than from injecting code into production (memory: main site is production).

No `requirements.md` in the task folder: the brief survives only inside the agent's transcript (`c174785d…jsonl`, first prompt). `session.jsonl` holds only the assign line, a commit and the stray `set` line, with no log, findings or outcome. A fresh agent could not continue from this folder.

`InFlight.real.test.mjs` doesn't test the bug that was fixed. It goes through node's `Session.replay` + `Task.resolver`, which already read the agent folder as running before this change, so it passes with or without the `Task.js:513` line. The browser path (`Task.open_ref`) is still untested.

The index is stale. The file table in `core/Session/doc/in-flight.md:14-19` doesn't list `InFlight.real.test.mjs`, `fixtures/` or `doc/in-flight-real-400.png`; they appear only in a dated "Real-page fix (2026-11-02)" history paragraph (`in-flight.md:36-38`), and readmes state structure, not history (law 9). `core/Task`'s readme/doc also says nothing about `open_ref` now inferring state at the end.

`doc/in-flight-real-400.png` shows "+ 34 more running" in one session, with several rows at 0% "starting". Once a spawned-agent folder with no verb line is inferred `running`, every dead or abandoned agent folder reads as in flight forever (e.g. `dictate-plugins`, whose last real line says its minion was stopped). The brief wanted the running ones; this may now over-count. Worth checking against `list_agents`.

`InFlightView.js:28` shows "Reading the session…" whenever `picks` is empty. That is also forever when a session's file never arrives (404), or on `/framework/ai/` when the inflight query returns zero rows (`AIDashboard.js:37` passes `urls: []`), where "Nothing is in flight." was the right answer.

The fix copies `Item.open`'s pattern (`attach` then `replay_end`, `Item.js:793-794`), but `open_ref`'s other branch (`Task.js:504-508`, a stub reading a snapshot when TaskPage already holds the store) still never calls `replay_end`, so the same agent folder reads idle there. Fixing it in one place would cover both branches.

Widths given: one shot at 400 (`doc/in-flight-real-400.png`, an element shot, no `layout.json`). It cuts off the "In flight" heading under the sticky site header, and the fixed bottom bar sits mid-image.
